title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting - Nature Energy
gist: EPFL researchers demonstrate the first organic-semiconductor photocatalyst sheet for unassisted solar water splitting: a single polymer bulk heterojunction acts as photocathode or photoanode depending on micropatterned molecular underlayers (2PACz/NI-PA) on FTO. The 1,000-µm-domain sheet reaches only 0.1% solar-to-hydrogen (1.3 µmol/h/cm2 H2, >2 h), versus 1.1% for inorganic sheets and an 11–17% theoretical ceiling, with smaller domains hurt by boundary recombination.

insights.claim: A single organic bulk heterojunction (polymer donor PBDTTTPD with polymer acceptor PNDIHDT) can act as either a photocathode for hydrogen evolution or a photoanode for oxygen evolution depending only on the molecular charge-selective layer beneath it.
